quote: The wide world is all about you: you can fence yourselves in, but you cannot for ever fence it out.
source: J. R. R. Tolkien, The Fellowship of the Ring, Book I, chapter 3, Three is Company (George Allen and Unwin, 1954) (Gildor Inglorion)
speaker: Gildor Inglorion

evidence.where: The passage as quoted in full, with its surrounding sentences on others dwelling in the Shire before and after hobbits, on the Tolkien commentary site hmturnbull.com, which cites Book I, chapter III and prints the colon and the two-word for ever; the printed Allen and Unwin text was not opened directly
evidence.edition: The Fellowship of the Ring, George Allen and Unwin, London, 1954
evidence.locator: Book I, chapter 3, Three is Company, Gildor's parting counsel to Frodo at Woodhall

reason: Gildor's line to Frodo in Three is Company, in the book's own wording with the colon and Tolkien's two-word for ever, which the proposal already carried; the Calendar For Life copy had modernised it to forever.
